title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: Generative faculty corrupted as moral tip
pass_a_gloss: From that depraved faculty came corrupt seed congruent with it and with the other powers the generative tries to imprint in the seed. How viciousness passes from seed to rational soul Placeus defers to GAR's last chapter, God granting. GAR presses what Placeus had pressed elsewhere: whence—Scripture or elsewhere—or is this curious fiction under a shade of subtlety? Placeus answers that he demanded revelation for GAR's internal divine act; here he claims nothing that Scripture, reason, or experience itself cannot firm. Tip before the moral-generative faculty quarrel.
pass_b_english: From a faculty so corrupted and acting depravedly a corrupt seed was wrought—that is, agreeable and congruent with the depraved generative faculty, and also with the other faculties which the generative power tries as accurately as possible to sketch and express in the seed. But how this viciousness passes from seed to the rational soul I will explain, God granting, in its place—that is, at the last chapter of your treatise. GAR. First we ask of him what he elsewhere asked of us: Whence do you have that? From the Scriptures, or from elsewhere? Or how do you show this is not to be counted among fictions which delight the curious with an empty shade of subtlety? PLAC. I asked whence you had it, when I was disputing, of what he said about a certain internal act of the divine mind and will, to be known from nowhere but divine revelation. But here what have I said of that sort which cannot be firmed by Scripture, or by reason, or by experience itself?
source_text: A facultate sic corrupta ac depravate agente elaboratum est semen corruptum, hoc est, consentaneum ac congruens cum depravata facultati generatrici, tum etiam aliis facultatibus quas generatrix semine adumbrare & exprimere quam accuratissime conatur. Quomodo autem haec vitiositas a semine ad animam rationalem transeat; suo loco, hoc est, ad Cap. ultimum tractatus tui Deo dante exponam. GAR. Primum id ab eo quaerimus, quod ipse a nobis alibi, Unde id habes? Ex Scripturisne, an aliunde? aut quomodo demonstras, hoc non esse inter figmenta habendum, quae inani subtilitatis umbra curiosulos delectant? PLAC. Quaesivi unde haberetis, qui cum disputabam, quod dicebat de interno quodam mentis & voluntatis divinae actu, non aliunde quam ex revelatione divina noscendo. Hic vero quid dixi eiusmodi, quod non vel Scriptura, vel ratione, vel experientia ipsa firmari possit?

choices.choice: Corrupt seed; GAR demands Scripture-source; Placeus: Scripture/reason/experience
